edges.why: The statement treats an attribute such as having four sides as a defining attribute that two named shapes can have in common.
To say two shapes share an attribute, the learner must pick out which shapes have a given attribute.
The test problem is answered by counting the sides of the rhombus and the rectangle and noting both have four.
A category defined by an attribute collects shapes of different named kinds that share that one attribute.
The statement says membership holds whatever the shape's other attributes, size, or orientation, which are non-defining.
The test problem asks the learner to pick out which listed shapes have the stated four-straight-sides attribute.
A quadrilateral is the polygon named by having exactly four sides, which this node extends to any shape.
The statement includes irregular, tilted, and inward-pointing figures, so size and orientation must not decide the name.
The definition names the rectangle as a quadrilateral, the figure with exactly four straight sides.
The defining attribute of a rectangle is that all four of its angles are right angles.
The definition names the rhombus as a quadrilateral, the figure with exactly four straight sides.
The defining attribute of a rhombus is that all four sides are equal in length.
The definition names the square as a quadrilateral, the figure with exactly four straight sides.
A square must have four sides of the same length, which is the equal-sides attribute.
A square must have four right angles, so a right angle must be recognized as a square corner.
The statement says a square stays a square in any orientation, such as standing on a corner.
The statement applies the definition of a rectangle to show it is a closed figure with four straight sides.
The statement applies the definition of a rhombus to show it is a closed figure with four straight sides.
The statement applies the definition of a square to show it is a closed figure with four straight sides.
The attribute that decides membership is exactly four straight sides, which defines a quadrilateral of any shape.
A shape that has the category attribute belongs to the category while keeping its own more specific name.

Step 2 makes two sides unequal so that the figure fails the equal-sides condition of a rhombus.
Step 3 makes one angle not right so that the figure fails the four-right-angles condition of a rectangle.
Step 4 checks the figure against the square definition of four equal sides and four right angles.
The statement says the corners of a figure are points, so the learner must identify the corners of a shape.
A line is named by two of its points, so the learner must know what a point is.
A segment is defined as the straight part of a line, so the meaning of a line is used.
A segment is bounded by two endpoints and named by them, and endpoints are points.
The statement identifies the sides of a polygon as segments, so the learner must identify sides of a shape.
A ray is defined as the part of a line that goes on without end in one direction.
A ray starts at one endpoint and is named starting with that endpoint, which is a point.
A right angle is a kind of angle, two rays from a common endpoint, whose sides form a square corner.
The statement describes the right angle as a square corner that fits the corner of a sheet of paper.
Acute and obtuse angles are defined by comparing their opening with the square corner of a right angle.
An obtuse angle must be smaller than a straight angle, whose two sides form a straight line.
The statement defines the drawn angle as two rays from a common endpoint.
Step 1 draws a ray, and later steps draw further rays from the same endpoint.
Step 2 places a square corner at the endpoint, and step 3 draws the right angle along its edge.
Steps 4 and 5 place the second ray inside or beyond the square corner according to the acute or obtuse comparison.
Perpendicularity is defined as a relationship between two lines that meet.
Two lines are perpendicular when the angles they form at the meeting point are right angles.
The statement extends the idea to segments and sides, which are perpendicular when the lines they lie on are.
The drawn line must satisfy the definition of being perpendicular to the given line.
Step 1 uses a square corner to produce the right angle at the given point.
Step 1 places the vertex of the square corner at the given point on the line.
Step 3 extends the drawn edge in both directions so that it becomes a line.
Parallel lines are lines that never meet however far they are extended in both directions without end.
The statement extends parallelism to segments and sides, which are parallel when their lines are.
The drawn line must satisfy the definition of never meeting the given line.
Step 1 slides a square corner along the line to draw a line at right angles to it.
Step 2 draws a line perpendicular, through the point, to the line drawn in step 1.
Step 3 explains the result because two lines perpendicular to the same line never meet.
Step 1 checks each pair of sides to see whether the lines they lie on are parallel.
Step 1 checks each pair of sides to see whether they meet at right angles.

Step 2 puts figures with an angle of the named type in one group and the others in another.
A right triangle is defined as a triangle with a right angle, a square corner.

The statement says right triangles form a category because they share the attribute of a right angle.
A line of symmetry is a line across the figure along which the figure is folded.
Folding along the line flips one part over onto the other part.
Matching exactly means the two parts, compared as whole shapes, are the same shape and size.
